note: Yemen, read on 2026-10-30 in Law No. 47 of 1991 on the entry and residence of foreigners (a Republican decree-law, published in the Official Gazette issue 7/7 of 1991), in the copy of the Yemeni laws kept by the University of Minnesota Human Rights Library (its text extracted from the PDF in Arabic presentation forms, which is how the quoted parts are written). Every foreigner must hold a residence licence (art. 17); foreigners are of three classes of residence, special, ordinary and temporary (art. 18). Special residence (art. 19) is given, besides two classes defined by years of residence before the law came into force, to scholars, men of letters, the arts, industry, economics and others who render great services to the country, by decision of the Minister of the Interior, licensed for ten years renewable on request: written as the talent route. Ordinary residence (art. 20) is only for those resident fifteen years before the law, so isn't a route for a newcomer and isn't written. Temporary residence (art. 22) is for everyone else, licensed for 'a most of one year' and renewable: written as a card for any purpose, its term left out, the form holding one length and not a most. As an exception the head of the Immigration, Passports and Naturalisation Authority may grant three years' residence, renewable, for the nature of the work, such as staff of oil companies and managers of companies and banks (art. 23): written as the work route with that term. The law leaves procedures, the time to apply, the forms and fees to the executive regulations and to ministerial decisions (arts. 24, 27, 29), which weren't found, so no fee, time or place to apply is written. Anyone employing a foreigner needs prior permission from the competent authorities (art. 15); the law doesn't say whether residence ties its holder to an employer, so `work` is left out. Nothing is read of a permanent status or of residence counting toward naturalisation. Whether the law has been amended since 1991 wasn't found: the Authority's own site (immigration.gov.ye) didn't answer today. The country's division since 2014 (two administrations each running immigration services) isn't modelled.
